summary: Iteration 5: Verified emailed-reset-link (Resend) password-reset flow for Squawk King IA. BACKEND (pytest 8/8 pass, /app/backend/tests/test_password_reset.py): (1) POST /api/auth/forgot-password with a KNOWN registered email returns 200 with generic body {message:'If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent.'} — no token/no code fields in the response; (2) POST /api/auth/forgot-password with an UNKNOWN email returns the SAME generic body (no enumeration); (3) full happy path: register -> forgot-password -> extract token from backend supervisor log line 'Resend not configured (placeholder key). Reset link for <email>: <origin>/reset?token=...' -> POST /api/auth/reset-password{token,new_password}=200/ok:true -> login with new password=200 -> login with old password=401 -> token reuse POST reset-password with same token = 400 'This reset link is invalid or has already been used.'; (4) short new_password (<6 chars) at /api/auth/reset-password = 400 'Password must be at least 6 characters'; (5) rate limit: 4 consecutive POSTs /api/auth/forgot-password for the SAME email in <15min -> 4th returns HTTP 429 'Too many reset requests…'; (6) regression: /api/auth/change-password still works (login with new pw = 200, login with old pw = 401); (7) regression: demo login mechanic@squawkking.io/squawk123 = 200; (8) regression: /api/auth/register new user = 200 (email is lowercased server-side — noted). FRONTEND (Playwright, 12/12 scenarios pass): (a) /login loads; clicking [data-testid=forgot-link] switches to forgot mode which shows ONLY email-input + auth-submit (label 'Send Reset Link') — password-input is NOT rendered (count=0), and no [data-testid=reset-code-display] exists; (b) submitting forgot with a known freshly registered email shows [data-testid=auth-info] 'If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent. Check your inbox.' and NO 6-digit number appears anywhere on the page (regex \b\d{6}\b matches nothing in body); (c) submitting forgot with an unknown email shows the SAME auth-info banner and no auth-error; (d) /reset with NO token renders [data-testid=reset-password-page] and [data-testid=reset-no-token] warning; (e) /reset?token=<real> renders [reset-password-input]+[reset-confirm-input]+[reset-submit] — mismatched entry surfaces [reset-error] 'Passwords do not match'; (f) valid matching new password submits -> [reset-success] visible -> auto-redirect to /login; (g) login with the NEW password succeeds and navigates to workspace (/); (h) visiting /reset with the SAME already-used token and submitting yields [reset-error] 'This reset link is invalid or has already been used.'; (i) trying to log in with the OLD password on /login triggers [auth-error] 'Invalid email or password'; (j) regression: demo login mechanic@squawkking.io/squawk123 -> workspace loads with UNLIMITED badge; (k) regression: [data-testid=change-password-btn] opens [change-password-modal] with 3 inputs; submitting current=squawk123 new=squawk1234 shows 'Password changed successfully' toast; test reverted the demo password back to squawk123 via API to keep reviewer creds stable; (l) reset link extraction from /var/log/supervisor/backend.*.log works (line format 'Reset link for <email>: <origin>/reset?token=<43-char urlsafe>').
critical_code_review_comments: server.py forgot_password(): rate-limit counter is inserted into db.reset_attempts BEFORE the user-existence check. That is correct for anti-enumeration and rate-limiting semantics, but the collection has no TTL index — reset_attempts rows accumulate forever. Consider a TTL index on ts (or scheduled cleanup) to avoid unbounded growth.

server.py send_reset_email(): when Resend key is a placeholder, the reset link is logged via logger.warning — including the full token. In production this is expected to be a real send, but be mindful that in dev logs any reader can complete the reset. Consider gating this log to only DEBUG level, or truncating the token in the log message (log the /reset?token=<HIDDEN> and store the token in a separate dev-only file/queue).
server.py reset_password(): does not guard against reusing the CURRENT password. Users could set new_password == old password; consider optional check via verify_password + reject.

Login.jsx keeps the previously entered email between mode toggles (register/forgot/login). That's usually desired, but note password state is also kept — after switchMode from register to forgot the retained password is unused but still in memory. Minor; consider clearing on mode change.

ResetPassword.jsx: form password minLength check is duplicated between server (>=6) and client. Fine, but the client check runs BEFORE the mismatch check — if a user enters 'a' twice mismatching, they get the length error first even though they typed matching characters. Acceptable UX.
ForgotInput.origin_url is a plain string; no URL validation. If a client posts junk, the resulting link in the log/email will be broken but harmless (no crash). Consider Pydantic HttpUrl.
The reset link in dev logs uses the caller's origin_url verbatim (echoed into the log). Not a security issue but a mildly noisy log if origin_url is malformed.
No cleanup or expiry sweep on password_reset_tokens collection — expired/used tokens persist indefinitely. Add a TTL index on expires_at.
test_credentials: Demo admin: mechanic@squawkking.io / squawk123. Frontend tests registered throwaway users like uitest_<hex>@example.com; test also temporarily changed demo password to squawk1234 and reverted to squawk123 via /api/auth/change-password so reviewer creds remain stable.
seed_data_creation: Registered several TEST_reset_*@example.com and uitest_*@example.com throwaway users during backend + UI runs. No cleanup performed — they are inert accounts and do not affect reviewer flows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Password-reset feature verified end-to-end. Selectors used and stable: [data-testid=forgot-link], [data-testid=auth-info], [data-testid=auth-error], [data-testid=auth-submit], [data-testid=back-to-login], [data-testid=reset-password-page], [data-testid=reset-no-token], [data-testid=reset-password-input], [data-testid=reset-confirm-input], [data-testid=reset-submit], [data-testid=reset-error], [data-testid=reset-success], [data-testid=change-password-btn], [data-testid=change-password-modal], [data-testid=change-password-submit]. To harvest a token in tests, grep 'reset link for <email>' from /var/log/supervisor/backend.out.log or backend.err.log and pull the ?token=... query param (43-char urlsafe). Rate limit is 3/15min per email — running the pytest twice in the same window against the same email will 429 on the 4th call; tests use fresh emails per case so this is stable. RESEND_API_KEY is intentionally the placeholder re_placeholder_change_me in dev — the logged-link fallback is expected behavior; do not report 'no email delivered' as a bug.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature verified working end-to-end. Only minor code-quality notes flagged under critical_code_review_comments (TTL indexes on reset_attempts and password_reset_tokens; log level of reset link).
